hits.draft_en:
If you can lose hours to something, you're probably not short on discipline. You just haven't pointed it anywhere yet.

I'm trying to point mine at one plain page a day.
hits.video_tip: 15s: hands holding a pen over a blank page, pause, then write one line. VO: 'Point it somewhere.' No music.

hits.name: Sahil Bloom
hits.text: I’m convinced that the key to overcoming anything is to shrink the time horizon. Just focus on the next hour. Do one thing that moves you forward. One closed loop. One workout. …
hits.hook: SahilBloom: shrink the time horizon to the next hour, one closed loop at a time
hits.draft_en:
When the whole thing feels too big, I shrink the clock.

Not this year. Not this month. The next hour.

One page written. One email answered. One small thing finished.

Then I look up and pick the next one. That's most of how anything has actually changed for me.
hits.video_tip: 20 to 30 seconds, overhead on the desk, natural light, room sound only. Set a phone timer for 60 minutes. Write 'Next hour:' on a plain page and one task under it. Start the timer, write, close the notebook. Text on screen: 'Shrink the clock.'

hits.name: James Clear
hits.text:
A Monday morning question for you: 

Always work on the limiting factor. 

What is holding you back right now?
hits.hook: jamesclear: Monday question, work on the limiting factor
hits.draft_en:
Monday question I'm answering on paper before the coffee goes cold:

What's the one thing actually holding this up?

It's usually smaller than I think. And I usually already know.
hits.video_tip: 15 to 20s: write the question by hand on a plain page, then one honest answer underneath. Hold on the page for 3 seconds.

reply_ideas.reply_text: The next hour is the only size that's ever worked for me. When I try to fix the whole year at once, I mostly end up making lists about the year. One closed loop, then the next. Good thing to read on a Monday.
I answer these on paper. A pen slows me down enough that the real answer shows up instead of the polite one. This morning's: [your honest limiting factor].
Distill is the word I needed today. Adding things has always felt like progress to me, and it mostly isn't. The page gets clear when I start crossing out.

"Would I go after this now if I didn't have it" works on plans too, not just things. I'm asking it about every idea for the small shop I'm building. Some of them don't make it, which is kind of the point.
